title: Crop Row Length Calculator: Rows and Total Feet
description: Work out row count and total row length for a field with the Crop Row Length Calculator — from field width, length and row spacing. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 20-acre field 660 ft wide planted at 30-inch spacing holds 264 rows — and 66.0 miles of total row in a single field.
quick_answer: The Crop Row Length Calculator turns a field's width, length and row spacing into the two numbers planting and spraying consume: how many rows the field holds, and total row length. Enter the three figures and read both — no paced estimates, no surprises at the seed order.
steps_intro: Rows are where fieldwork is measured — in feet and miles, not acres. Three inputs:

body.t: Seed quantity follows row length and in-row spacing. Total row feet from this calculator is the input the seed maths needs — acres alone cannot give it.

body.t: Drip tape and mulch film are bought by the foot of row. A 66-mile answer changes the order from guesswork to a quantity.

Wider spacing means fewer, longer-lasting rows; narrower means more row-miles per field. The trade is visible in one calculation each way.

Field 1,320 × 660 ft (exactly 20.0 acres), rows along the long side at 30-inch (2.5 ft) spacing: 660 ÷ 2.5 = 264 rows, each 1,320 ft — total 348,480 ft = 66.0 miles of row. A single field, a marathon × 2.5 of row.
The same field at 36-inch spacing: 220 rows, 55.0 miles total. The spacing decision moves total row length by eleven miles — which is why it is made with a calculator, not a habit.

faq: From field width, field length and row spacing: the number of rows that fit across the width, and the total row length (rows × length), in feet and miles.
No — the calculation is instant and free, like the rest of the site.
Can I use the result for professional work?
Yes, for ordering and planning. It assumes straight parallel rows across a rectangular field; irregular fields should be split into rectangles and summed.
Which width do the rows run along?
Rows are counted across the field's width and run along its length — swap the two inputs if your rows run the other way; the calculator follows the convention you enter.
The geometric answer does not; subtract your headland allowance from the row length before ordering materials if your turns eat into the planted length.

The same division works in metres: width ÷ spacing (in metres) = rows; rows × length = total metres. A 200 m-wide field at 0.75 m spacing holds 266 rows (rounding down — partial rows are not planted).
Why miles of row in one field?
Because implements travel rows, not acres. Row-miles are the unit fuel, time and wear actually accumulate in.
Rows run the short way — what changes?

Swap width and length: rows are counted across the dimension they run perpendicular to. The total row length is the same product either way only if spacing is counted across the other side — check which side your planter crosses.
How does this help with planter calibration?
Seed per foot of row × total row feet = seed for the field. This total is the multiplier every per-row rate needs.
